summary: On node1, created user datauser and directory /srv/data, enabled XFS project quota on the root filesystem (rootflags=pquota via grubby + fstab), assigned project id 100 to /srv/data mapped to datauser, and set a 100MB hard block limit via xfs_quota. Enforcement verified: a 50MB write succeeded, a subsequent 80MB write was rejected by the kernel with ENOSPC once usage hit exactly 100M. Test files were cleaned up afterward, restoring quota usage to 0. The mandatory single-node restart protocol was executed: captured pre-reboot boot_id (5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc), issued a non-interactive systemctl reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (22bbbbcb-f435-4986-8134-570a1acfe893) proving an actual restart, and verified sshd active and root filesystem healthy (mounted with prjquota, 5% used) post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS, filesystem (XFS root, no separate /srv/data mount), and existing quota tooling
Created local user datauser and directory /srv/data (owned by datauser, mode 750)
Set kernel rootflags=pquota via grubby for all kernels and updated /etc/fstab root entry to include pquota
Rebooted node1 via non-interactive `systemctl reboot`, ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed changed boot_id
Verified root filesystem remounted with prjquota option
Configured XFS project 100 mapped to /srv/data and named it 'datauser' via /etc/projects, /etc/projid, and `xfs_quota project -s`
Set 100MB hard block limit for the datauser project via `xfs_quota limit -p bhard=100m`
Demonstrated enforcement: 50MB write by datauser succeeded, subsequent 80MB write failed with ENOSPC at exactly 100M used
Cleaned up test files and re-verified quota usage reset to 0 and node health (sshd active, root fs mounted normally)

evidence.requirement: Baseline filesystem/user state before changes (no datauser, /srv/data absent, root xfs mounted noquota)
evidence.summary: Showed root fs is XFS mounted with explicit noquota, /srv/data and datauser did not yet exist

evidence.requirement: Pre-reboot setup: user/dir creation and pquota kernel/fstab configuration, plus pre-restart boot_id baseline
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 5fb1b173-...; created datauser and /srv/data; set grubby rootflags=pquota; updated /etc/fstab to add pquota option

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement for node1 (single node, native reboot mechanism, ack before disconnect)
evidence.summary: Issued `systemctl reboot` in background with disown; stream closed as node went down, evidencing the reboot was accepted

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 restart completed and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node offline during reboot); second poll succeeded and returned new boot_id 22bbbbcb-..., differing from the pre-reboot 5fb1b173-... baseline

evidence.requirement: Filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser under /srv/data, configured and proven with actual writes
evidence.summary: Confirmed root remounted with prjquota; set project 100 (datauser) on /srv/data with 100M hard limit; 50MB write succeeded, 80MB write hit kernel ENOSPC exactly at 100M used, proving filesystem-level enforcement

evidence.requirement: Post-restart cluster/node health and cleanup verification
evidence.summary: Removed test files, confirmed quota usage returned to 0/100M, sshd active, root filesystem healthy at 5% used, and re-confirmed post-restart boot_id 22bbbbcb-...
